answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can force each key to keep a private juniper storage shard derived from its address and the epoch seed, sized at 200 MB that must stay online. Every epoch a random beacon picks two byte ranges; the key must return them in under three seconds to earn its nectar payout. Missed or shared shards slash the key for ten epochs. One honest agent holds 200 MB once; 1,000 fakes need 200 TB held continuously and 1,000 separate live replies. Limit: low-resource keys get a smaller shard and a slower payout ramp.
